\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Invariance — Smoothing}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.Smoothing
\section{Overview}
Interval averaging gives quantitative smooth approximations of Lipschitz functions. Fourth-derivative expectation comparisons imply Lipschitz comparisons with an explicit constant.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Translated interval average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth}
\leanok
For real $\eta,x$ and any real function $\psi$, the interval smoothing is $S_\eta\psi(x)=\eta^{-1}\int_0^\eta\psi(x+t)\,dt$, with value zero for $\eta=0$. The integral is oriented when $\eta<0$ and is assigned zero when its integrand is not integrable.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative of a translated interval average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth_hasDerivAt}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\eta>0$ and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. For every $x\in\mathbb
R$, the translated interval average $S_\eta\psi$ is differentiable at $x$, with
derivative $\bigl(\psi(x+\eta)-\psi(x)\bigr)/\eta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Regularity gained by interval smoothing]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.contDiff_intervalSmooth}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth_hasDerivAt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\eta>0$, let $m\in\mathbb N$, and let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be
$m$-times continuously differentiable. Then $S_\eta\psi$ is $(m+1)$-times continuously
differentiable on $\mathbb R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Higher derivatives of an interval average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.iteratedDeriv_intervalSmooth}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth_hasDerivAt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\beta>0$, let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $\psi:\bbr\to\bbr$ be $m$ times
continuously differentiable. For the interval average
$S_\beta\psi(x)=\beta^{-1}\int_0^\beta \psi(x+t)\,dt$, its $(m+1)$st derivative at every
$x\mathbin\bbr$ is $((\psi^{(m)}(x+\beta)-\psi^{(m)}(x))/\beta)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative bound for interval smoothing]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.abs_deriv_intervalSmooth_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth_hasDerivAt}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\eta>0$, let $c\ge0$, and let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $c$-Lipschitz.
For every $x\in\mathbb R$, the interval smoothing $S_\eta\psi$ satisfies
$\left|(S_\eta\psi)'(x)\right|\le c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Interval averaging preserves the Lipschitz constant]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_intervalSmooth}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.abs_deriv_intervalSmooth_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth_hasDerivAt}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\eta>0$ and define the interval average of $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ by
\[
S_\eta\psi(x)=\frac1\eta\int_0^\eta\psi(x+t)\,dt.
\]
If $\psi$ is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$, then $S_\eta\psi$ is also $c$-Lipschitz.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Approximation by interval smoothing]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.abs_intervalSmooth_sub_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\eta>0$, let $c\ge0$, and let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $c$-Lipschitz.
For every $x\in\mathbb R$, $|S_\eta\psi(x)-\psi(x)|\le c\eta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Regularity and bounds for repeated interval averaging]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth_iterate_bounds}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.abs_deriv_intervalSmooth_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.abs_intervalSmooth_sub_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.contDiff_intervalSmooth, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.iteratedDeriv_intervalSmooth, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_intervalSmooth}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\eta>0$, let $c\ge0$, and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $c$-Lipschitz. For
each natural number $m$, set $\phi=S_\eta^{m+1}\psi$, the result of applying the
translated interval average $m+1$ times. Then $\phi$ is $m+1$ times continuously
differentiable and $c$-Lipschitz, and for every $x\in\mathbb R$,
\[|\phi(x)-\psi(x)|\le(m+1)c\eta,\qquad |\phi^{(m+1)}(x)|\le c(2/\eta)^m.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth-order smooth approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.exists_contDiff_four_approx}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth_iterate_bounds}
\difficulty{4}
For every real $\eta>0$, every nonnegative real number $c$, and every $c$-Lipschitz
function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, there exists a function $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb
R$ of class $C^4$ such that, for every real $x$, $|\phi(x)-\psi(x)|\le 4c\eta$ and
$|\phi^{(4)}(x)|\le 8c/\eta^3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation stability under uniform approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.abs_integral_sub_le_uniform}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $f,g\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ with
$f$ integrable and $g$ measurable up to a null set. If $D\in\mathbb R$ satisfies
$|f(\omega)-g(\omega)|\le D$ for every $\omega\in\Omega$, then $\left|\int f\,d\mu-\int
g\,d\mu\right|\le D$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lipschitz comparison at a smoothing scale]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_expectation_bound_at_scale}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.abs_integral_sub_le_uniform, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.exists_contDiff_four_approx, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp_four}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let $U\in L^4(\mu)$ and
$V\in L^4(\nu)$. Suppose $B\ge0$ and, for every $C^4$ function $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb
R$ and every $C\ge0$ such that $|\phi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, assume
\[
\left|\int \phi(U)\,d\mu-\int \phi(V)\,d\nu\right|\le CB.
\]
Then for every $c\ge0$, every $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, and
every $\eta>0$,
\[
\left|\int \psi(U)\,d\mu-\int \psi(V)\,d\nu\right|\le 8c\eta+\frac{8c}{\eta^3}B.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lipschitz comparison from fourth derivative bounds]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_expectation_bound_of_fourth_derivative}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lipschitz_expectation_bound_at_scale}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let $U\in L^4(\mu)$ and
$V\in L^4(\nu)$. Suppose $B\ge0$ and, for every $C^4$ function $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb
R$ and every $C\ge0$ such that $|\phi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, assume
\[
\left|\int \phi(U)\,d\mu-\int \phi(V)\,d\nu\right|\le CB.
\]
Then for every $c\ge0$ and every $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
\[
\left|\int \psi(U)\,d\mu-\int \psi(V)\,d\nu\right|\le16cB^{1/4}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\section{Additional declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Continuity of iterated interval smoothing]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.continuous_intervalSmooth_iterate}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.continuous_intervalSmooth_iterate}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.contDiff_intervalSmooth, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\eta>0$, let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let $m\in\mathbb
N$. The result of applying the interval smoothing $S_\eta$ to $\psi$ repeatedly $m$
times is continuous on $\mathbb R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Value attained by a repeated interval average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth_iterate_exists_value}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth_iterate_exists_value}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.continuous_intervalSmooth_iterate, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.intervalSmooth}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\eta>0$ and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. For every natural
number $m$ and every real $x$, there is a point $y\in[x,x+m\eta]$ such that
$S_\eta^m\psi(x)=\psi(y)$.
\end{theorem}
